blurred-frame-maker.name: Blurred Frame Maker
blurred-frame-maker.tagline: The Instagram square look, no cropping.
blurred-frame-maker.metaTitle: Blurred Frame Maker - Square Photos Without Cropping | JaurTools
blurred-frame-maker.metaDescription: Fit any photo into a square with a soft blurred background — the classic Instagram look. Free, no crop.
blurred-frame-maker.keywords: blurred frame image, blur background photo, square crop instagram, whatsapp dp maker, blurred border photo
blurred-frame-maker.quickAnswer: Upload a landscape or portrait photo and pick a target ratio — 1:1 for Instagram posts, 9:16 for stories and WhatsApp status. The tool builds a canvas at that ratio, fills it with a blurred, stretched copy of your photo, then centers the sharp original on top. A 1200 x 800 photo at 1:1 becomes a 1080 x 1080 image with the sharp 1080 x 720 photo floating over blurred bands.
keyFacts: The background is your own photo, blurred and stretched to cover the whole canvas — no awkward empty bars.
Blur radius 0 to 60 px controls how dreamy the background looks.
The dim slider darkens the background so the sharp photo pops forward.
The sharp layer is never cropped or stretched — it fits fully inside the frame.
Output is a PNG sized for crisp social uploads.
howTo: Upload any photo — landscape, portrait, or square.
Choose the target ratio for where you will post it.
Drag the blur slider until the background looks smooth and stylish.
Use the dim slider if the background competes with your photo.
Click Download to save the framed image as PNG.
blurred-frame-maker.formula:
Canvas: side = 1080 px base, scaled by ratio.
For ratio a:b: canvasWidth = 1080 x a / max(a,b), canvasHeight = 1080 x b / max(a,b).
Background: the photo drawn stretched to cover the full canvas, then blurred with radius R.
Foreground: the photo scaled to fit inside the canvas (contain), centered.
Example: 1:1 -> 1080 x 1080 canvas.
blurred-frame-maker.workedExample:
Photo 1200 x 800, ratio 1:1, blur 25:
1. Canvas: 1080 x 1080.
2. Background: the 1200 x 800 photo stretched to cover 1080 x 1080, then blurred with radius 25.
3. Foreground: the photo scaled by 1080/1200 = 0.9 to 1080 x 720, centered vertically.
4. Result: sharp 1080 x 720 photo with 180 px tall blurred bands above and below — no black bars, no cropping.
benefits: Post landscape shots as square posts without cropping anything out.
Blurred fills look far more professional than black or white bars.
One tool covers Instagram, WhatsApp status, and story formats.
Dim control keeps busy backgrounds from stealing attention.
No account, no watermark — the PNG is clean and yours.
limitations: The background is a blurred copy — it cannot show anything the photo does not contain.
Output is capped at 1080 px on the long side for fast processing.
Very dark photos make dim backgrounds nearly invisible; raise blur instead.
Square photos gain nothing from 1:1 mode — pick 9:16 or 4:5 for a visible effect.
blurred-frame-maker.privacyNote: This tool runs 100% in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.

faqs.q: Why not just crop my photo to a square?
faqs.a: Cropping a landscape photo to a square throws away the left and right thirds. The blurred frame keeps 100 percent of your photo visible and fills the leftover space with a stylish blurred extension of itself.
1:1 for Instagram feed posts and profile pictures, 4:5 for taller feed posts, 9:16 for Instagram/Facebook stories and WhatsApp status, 16:9 for YouTube thumbnails and cover photos.

faqs.q: Will the sharp photo be stretched?
faqs.a: Never. The sharp layer uses contain scaling, which preserves the exact aspect ratio. Only the blurred background copy is stretched, and blur hides the stretch.
20 to 35 px suits most photos — enough to hide the stretch but still show colors and shapes. Below 10 the background can look like a printing error; above 45 it melts into pure color wash.

faqs.q: Can I use this for a WhatsApp DP?
faqs.a: Yes — WhatsApp crops profile pictures to a square, so generate at 1:1 and your whole photo survives inside the DP circle instead of being cropped.

faqs.q: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faqs.a: No. The frame is composited on a canvas in your browser. Your photo never leaves your device.
